bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- First-mover/pioneer of Integrated Starter Generators (ISG) in India and Sensorless ISG globally; ~35% of India's 2&3-wheeler production in FY26 used ISG, ~40% of that with SEDEMAC's Sensorless ISG

- Dominant position in generator controls — products used on over 75% of the Indian generator market and over 15% of the global generator market
- High talent density technical team: ~237 engineers at FY26-end, over 60% (154) from IITs/NITs/BITS, with a 'technical nucleus' of promoters and senior engineers contributing 200+ man-years
- ISG technology used by three of the top four 2&3-wheeler OEMs in India and on four of the top-10 2-wheeler models sold in India in FY26
- Manufacturing facilities certified to ISO 9001 and IATF standards supporting high-volume, quality-consistent production
- Reducing customer concentration risk via ISG adoption by OEMs beyond the anchor customer and ramp-up of EFI ECU sales to a North American genset OEM
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — TVS Motor Company is the single most significant customer, having adopted the SLC-based ISG proposition since 2018 — The Chairman's Key Risks section states that rapid market expansion of an innovative proposition relies on anchor early adopters and 'often results in a situation of customer concentration'. The company's own concentration measure — revenue from the biggest customer minus the sum of the next four customers — was 72% in FY 2023-24, 68% in FY 2024-25 and 58% in FY 2025-26. Management names Sensorless ISG penetration plus growth in Commercial Vehicles and Power Tools as the levers expected to lower this only in the mid-term, so a single OEM's model cycle or sourcing decision remains the dominant swing factor on revenue.
- Electrification of the Indian 2&3-wheeler market, plus OEM vertical integration, against a revenue base historically dependent on engine-powered 2&3-wheelers — The AR states that because revenue has historically had a high dependence on supply of products for engine-powered 2&3-wheelers, a shift of the Indian 2&3-wheeler industry towards electrification poses a risk to the business. Management frames two primary questions: whether it has compelling propositions for electric 2&3-wheelers, and whether OEM thinking on vertical integration would reduce the size of its addressable market. Migration to date is early: products supplied to the electric 2&3-wheeler market rose from 0.3% of 2&3-wheeler revenue in FY 2023-24 to 1.7% in FY 2024-25 to 7.4% in FY 2025-26 — broadly only in line with the EV share of the Indian 2-wheeler market, i.e. tracking the shift rather than out-running it.
- Dependence on continued success in developing and commercialising substantial new technology propositions — failure at any stage of the innovation pipeline caps new-market entry — Management states success has historically depended on introducing innovative technology that unlocks new markets (smart ignition for carburetted 2&3-wheeler engines, electronic governing in genset controllers, SLC motor control without position sensors), and that each new proposition must pass a defined sequence — technology proposition and proof of concept, commercial business win, initial introduction, early growth, broader market adoption, sustaining industry proposition. Each stage introduces distinct risks and 'any failure at any stage, whether due to technical, commercial, operational, or market-related factors, can limit our ability to open new markets and grow our business.' This is the structural counterpart to the concentration risk: the de-concentration plan itself depends on the pipeline converting.
- Input-cost inflation and tightening semiconductor supply chains flagged as a near-term dampener on EBITDA margin — In the FY 2026-27 Outlook, management names commodity price inflation due to geopolitical instability together with tightening semiconductor supply chains as a factor that could raise raw material costs and 'may create mild pressure on EBITDA margin in the near term'. Material cost is the company's dominant expense line, so semiconductor availability and pricing sit directly on the gross margin for an electronics control-unit business with limited near-term pricing offset disclosed.
- Weather-driven demand exposure in both principal end markets — a strong El Nino in CY2026 threatening the Indian monsoon and the US hurricane season simultaneously — The FY 2026-27 Outlook names as the second potential dampener that forecasts of a strong El Nino in CY2026 raise the possibility of a weaker Indian monsoon and a less active US hurricane season, which could negatively affect India's 2-wheeler market and the US home-standby generator market respectively. Both of the company's demand pools are therefore exposed to the same climate driver in the same year. Management characterises both as global factors affecting the industry at large and states it does not see either as a structural threat.
- New-market/new-product ramps concentrated in a narrow set of OEM model wins, including the North American genset default adoption — The growth that is reducing customer concentration is itself lodged in a small number of specific design wins: ISG adoption in two more of the top-4 Indian OEMs 'including on some key models' over FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, the EFI ECU adopted as default by the North American genset market leader in their key model in FY 2025-26, and an FY 2026-27 expectation of introduction on variants of three top-10 2-wheeler models across three of the top four OEMs. The electric-machine foray (rare-earth-free motor plus MCU) is described as an emerging mid-long-term opportunity whose contribution is contingent — 'if our electric machine foray works out well'. Slippage in any one model programme moves a disproportionate share of the growth.
- First-year listed-company risk governance — the Risk Management Committee was constituted only on 13th October, 2025, months before the 11th March, 2026 listing — The Corporate Governance Report records the Risk Management Committee as constituted on 13th October, 2025 under Regulation 21, with a mandate spanning financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability, information and cyber security risks, business continuity planning, risk tolerance and appetite levels, and a policy review cadence of at least once in two years. Cyber security is singled out repeatedly in the terms of reference (framework for identification, implementing and monitoring policies and processes). The framework is therefore newly stood up rather than seasoned: the equity shares listed on 11th March, 2026, and the Stakeholders Relationship Committee held no meeting at all in the stub period to 31st March, 2026, so there is not yet a track record of the risk apparatus operating through a full listed cycle.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Grow into a global leader in ECUs for small powertrains by leveraging synergy across seemingly unrelated markets — 2&3-wheelers (ICE and electric), Power Tools, small Commercial Vehicles, small Tractors, Small Generators and Outdoor Powered Equipment.
- Commonize motor-controller components and designs across these small-powertrain markets (similar power/voltage ratings) to accumulate volumes and gain sourcing/supply-chain scale benefits.
- Extend the ISG+EFI combined ECU proposition to accelerate the ICE-powered 2&3-wheeler market's shift towards adopting ISG as a default.
- Move into manufacturing electric machines/motors — starting with 2&3-wheeler ISG systems and extending to an integrated rare-earth-free motor with MCU for electric 2&3-wheelers and e-bicycles — as a complementary opportunity to the core ECU business.
- Lower customer concentration risk by broadening ISG adoption beyond the anchor customer and growing in new markets (Commercial Vehicles, Power Tools).
- Address 2&3-wheeler electrification risk by leveraging existing motor-controller manufacturing scale, sourcing relationships and SLC technology (applicable to electric 2-wheelers, including eliminating Hall-sensor failure issues in hub-motor drives) to build compelling electric 2&3-wheeler propositions.
- Sustain a technical nucleus of promoters and senior engineers to continue generating and commercializing new, differentiated technology propositions across existing and new markets.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: SEDEMAC currently operates two manufacturing facilities dedicated to electronic controllers — MF1 in Chakan, Pune and MF2 in Wadgaon, Pune (both ISO 9001 and IATF certified) — through which it delivered its FY26 volume growth. The Company is in a phase of rapid manufacturing expansion: MF3 (Chakan, Pune, primarily electronic controllers) is under construction with significant progress made during the year and is scheduled to commence operations in Q2 of FY 2026-27, more than doubling available production area; MF4 (Chakan, Pune) is being operationalized for production of electric machines/motors. A major milestone during the year was the acquisition of industrial land at Shoolagiri, near Hosur, Tamil Nadu, intended to serve South India customers and provide long-term capacity expansion potential and geographic diversification. On the R&D side, the Company established a second technical development centre, TC2 in Pune (alongside existing TC1), increasing laboratory space for technology/product development and validation by approximately 60% to support its expanding engineering team. The Company is also broadening its engineering capability beyond electronic controllers into electromechanical/mechatronic products, with electric motors integrated with gearboxes for ISG applications set to be the first mechanically-intensive products from this expanded capability to enter production. For FY 2026-27, alongside the MF3 commissioning, management plans to strengthen its digital backbone for scalability and cyber-resilience.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rapid penetration of Sensorless ISG technology into India's engine-powered 2&3-wheeler market — ISG-equipped 2&3-wheeler production in India rose from ~7.1 million (FY25) to 8.4 million (FY26), with SEDEMAC capturing over 80% of the incremental volume growth.
- ISG and ISG+EFI ECUs now adopted by three of the top-4 2&3-wheeler manufacturers in India and used on five of the top-10 selling 2-wheelers in FY26; management views the ISG proposition as now in the 'broader market adoption' phase.
- Ramp-up of ISG+EFI ECU (integrating ISG and EFI electronics for cost-effectiveness) expected to make the ISG proposition more compelling for further OEM adoption.
- Electric 2&3-wheeler MCU revenue (3-wheeler MCU ramping since FY25; 2-wheeler MCU into series production in FY26) rose to 7.4% of Mobility revenue, broadly tracking EV penetration in the Indian 2-wheeler market.
- Industrial segment growth driven by market launch and ramp-up of the EFI ECU with the dominant North America genset market leader.
- Customer concentration (top customer minus next four) has been declining — 72% (FY24) to 68% (FY25) to 58% (FY26) — as ISG adoption broadens across OEMs and EFI ECU is adopted by a North American genset leader.
- New market development in Commercial Vehicles (engine and exhaust after-treatment controllers, motor controllers) and Power Tools (SLC-based MCU) expected to open additional growth avenues and further reduce customer/market concentration.
- Manufacturing footprint expansion (MF3 for ECUs, MF4 for electric motors, both in Chakan; land secured at Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu) undertaken to support current and future business growth.
- Commercial Vehicles: development of engine and exhaust gas after-treatment controllers and motor controllers continued through FY26; start of production expected over FY 2026-27.
- Power Tools: first business win secured with a small but established manufacturer for an SLC-based MCU; start of production expected over the next four to five quarters.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: SEDEMAC delivered a breakout FY26 with 61% revenue growth to INR 1,058 Cr, driven by regulatory-mandated ISG adoption in 2/3-wheelers and robust industrial genset demand. The investment case hinges on the proprietary sensorless control technology enabling cost-effective integration (ISG+EFI) and expansion into high-volume power tools and commercial vehicles, funding organic capex with >40% RoCE.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Indian Tier-I supplier selling directly to OEMs, with end-to-end in-house ownership of all four design layers - hardware, base software, application software and mechanical integration - and of engineering and manufacturing, without dependence on third-party licensors, technology partners or outsourcing. Design and validation run out of two Pune technical centres (TC1, TC2); manufacturing out of two Pune plants, MF1 (Chakan, control-intensive products) and MF2 (Wadgaon, non-critical products), with MF3 (Chakan, 80,000 sq.ft.) under construction, MF4 (Chakan, 9,300 sq.ft., electric motors) with its line set-up under process, and 13.45 acres allotted at SIPCOT Hosur, Tamil Nadu on a 99-year lease. Backward integration stops at component procurement: semiconductor components, printed circuit boards, die-cast metal and plastic parts, casings and motors are bought in, with part selection and commercials settled directly with the global manufacturers while deliveries flow through their distribution channels (Avnet, Rabyte, Arrow, Inno Circuits, SMET, WPG and others). Semiconductor components were 79.67%, 77.61%, 76.25% and 74.22% of cost of materials consumed in Fiscals 2023, 2024, 2025 and the nine months ended December 31, 2025; imported raw materials were 52.62%, 54.00%, 45.97% and 43.47% of revenue from operations over the same periods, all on purchase orders rather than long-term contracts. Forward integration is absent - the company does not sell to end users; its controllers are integrated into OEM equipment and shipped through the OEM sales channels, and as a B2B player it does not invest in direct advertising. R&D spend was 10.28%, 9.51%, 6.74% and 6.98% of revenue from operations across the same periods. cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Indian Tier-I supplier selling directly to OEMs, with end-to-end in-house ownership of all four design layers - hardware, base software, application software and mechanical integration - and of engineering and manufacturing, without dependence on third-party licensors, technology partners or outsourcing. Design and validation run out of two Pune technical centres (TC1, TC2); manufacturing out of two Pune plants, MF1 (Chakan, control-intensive products) and MF2 (Wadgaon, non-critical products), with MF3 (Chakan, 80,000 sq.ft.) under construction, MF4 (Chakan, 9,300 sq.ft., electric motors) with its line set-up under process, and 13.45 acres allotted at SIPCOT Hosur, Tamil Nadu on a 99-year lease. Backward integration stops at component procurement: semiconductor components, printed circuit boards, die-cast metal and plastic parts, casings and motors are bought in, with part selection and commercials settled directly with the global manufacturers while deliveries flow through their distribution channels (Avnet, Rabyte, Arrow, Inno Circuits, SMET, WPG and others). Semiconductor components were 79.67%, 77.61%, 76.25% and 74.22% of cost of materials consumed in Fiscals 2023, 2024, 2025 and the nine months ended December 31, 2025; imported raw materials were 52.62%, 54.00%, 45.97% and 43.47% of revenue from operations over the same periods, all on purchase orders rather than long-term contracts. Forward integration is absent - the company does not sell to end users; its controllers are integrated into OEM equipment and shipped through the OEM sales channels, and as a B2B player it does not invest in direct advertising. R&D spend was 10.28%, 9.51%, 6.74% and 6.98% of revenue from operations across the same periods. Government incentives (Duty Drawback, RoDTEP, Maharashtra Electronics Policy 2016 and M-SIPS) contributed 0.76%, 1.18%, 0.35% and 0.91% of revenue from operations.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rapid penetration of Sensorless ISG technology into India's engine-powered 2&3-wheeler market — ISG-equipped 2&3-wheeler production in India rose from ~7.1 million (FY25) to 8.4 million (FY26), with SEDEMAC capturing over 80% of the incremental volume growth.
- ISG and ISG+EFI ECUs now adopted by three of the top-4 2&3-wheeler manufacturers in India and used on five of the top-10 selling 2-wheelers in FY26; management views the ISG proposition as now in the 'broader market adoption' phase.
- Ramp-up of ISG+EFI ECU (integrating ISG and EFI electronics for cost-effectiveness) expected to make the ISG proposition more compelling for further OEM adoption.
- Electric 2&3-wheeler MCU revenue (3-wheeler MCU ramping since FY25; 2-wheeler MCU into series production in FY26) rose to 7.4% of Mobility revenue, broadly tracking EV penetration in the Indian 2-wheeler market.
- Industrial segment growth driven by market launch and ramp-up of the EFI ECU with the dominant North America genset market leader.
- Customer concentration (top customer minus next four) has been declining — 72% (FY24) to 68% (FY25) to 58% (FY26) — as ISG adoption broadens across OEMs and EFI ECU is adopted by a North American genset leader.
- New market development in Commercial Vehicles (engine and exhaust after-treatment controllers, motor controllers) and Power Tools (SLC-based MCU) expected to open additional growth avenues and further reduce customer/market concentration.
- Manufacturing footprint expansion (MF3 for ECUs, MF4 for electric motors, both in Chakan; land secured at Shoolagiri, Tamil Nadu) undertaken to support current and future business growth.
- Commercial Vehicles: development of engine and exhaust gas after-treatment controllers and motor controllers continued through FY26; start of production expected over FY 2026-27.
- Power Tools: first business win secured with a small but established manufacturer for an SLC-based MCU; start of production expected over the next four to five quarters.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: SEDEMAC currently operates two manufacturing facilities dedicated to electronic controllers — MF1 in Chakan, Pune and MF2 in Wadgaon, Pune (both ISO 9001 and IATF certified) — through which it delivered its FY26 volume growth. The Company is in a phase of rapid manufacturing expansion: MF3 (Chakan, Pune, primarily electronic controllers) is under construction with significant progress made during the year and is scheduled to commence operations in Q2 of FY 2026-27, more than doubling available production area; MF4 (Chakan, Pune) is being operationalized for production of electric machines/motors. A major milestone during the year was the acquisition of industrial land at Shoolagiri, near Hosur, Tamil Nadu, intended to serve South India customers and provide long-term capacity expansion potential and geographic diversification. On the R&D side, the Company established a second technical development centre, TC2 in Pune (alongside existing TC1), increasing laboratory space for technology/product development and validation by approximately 60% to support its expanding engineering team. The Company is also broadening its engineering capability beyond electronic controllers into electromechanical/mechatronic products, with electric motors integrated with gearboxes for ISG applications set to be the first mechanically-intensive products from this expanded capability to enter production. For FY 2026-27, alongside the MF3 commissioning, management plans to strengthen its digital backbone for scalability and cyber-resilience.

one-line thesis: SEDEMAC delivered a breakout FY26 with 61% revenue growth to INR 1,058 Cr, driven by regulatory-mandated ISG adoption in 2/3-wheelers and robust industrial genset demand. The investment case hinges on the proprietary sensorless control technology enabling cost-effective integration (ISG+EFI) and expansion into high-volume power tools and commercial vehicles, funding organic capex with >40% RoCE.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,058 Cr (+61% YoY); EBITDA: >INR 200 Cr (~21% margin, up due to operating leverage); PAT: >INR 100 Cr (normalized, no major one-offs cited); Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but implied strong via 3.9M units sold (+60% YoY); Net Debt: Low leverage implied by funding growth via internal accruals and modest working capital intensity.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Continued double-digit growth expected from new motorcycle launches (3 top-10 models) and EV MCU ramp; Margin: Mild pressure expected from commodity inflation and semiconductor tightness; Order Inflow: Strong visibility from ISG+EFI integration and export 3W ramp; Capex: MF3 (ECU) commissioning Q2FY27, MF4 (Electric Machines) Q3FY27.
order book & pipeline: Proxy via unit sales: 3.9 million control-intensive ECUs in FY26 (+60% YoY); 80% of incremental ISG volume in India captured by SEDEMAC; SOP achieved for export 3W ISG in Q4FY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mobility: Dominant in ICE 2/3W ISG (OBD-II driver), ramping EV MCUs (e2W/e3W); Industrial: Genset controllers (North America market share gain via default adoption by leader); New: Power tools (first biz win, SOP in 4-5 quarters), Commercial Vehicle after-treatment (SOP H2FY27).
growth verticals / optionality: Power tools market (300M units/year potential); Sensorless EV MCU global differentiation; ISG+EFI integrated unit adoption reducing OEM BOM; Export penetration beyond Indian OEM exports to direct global Japanese/Chinese OEMs.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin ~21%; Near-term headwinds from commodity inflation and semiconductor supply tightness expected to cause mild margin pressure; Long-term margins protected by proprietary sensorless tech and high switching costs.
capex / expansion: Cumulative plant capex INR 227 Cr (as of Mar-25); MF3 (120k sq ft, 3x ECU capacity) shipments Q2FY27; MF4 (Electric Machines) shipments Q3FY27; Land acquired in Shoolagiri for southern India presence; Capex intensity ~20-22% of incremental revenue.
capital allocation: Growth funded primarily by internal accruals (EBIT ~15%); Working capital intensity ~13-15% of revenue; No dividend discussion; Focus on reinvestment for capacity and R&D (cumulative INR 256 Cr).
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration (top 1 minus next 4 metric improving but still relevant); Commodity/semiconductor cost inflation; El Nino impact on monsoon (domestic 2W demand) and US hurricanes (genset demand); R&D execution risk in new segments (CV, Power Tools).
management quality / tone: Confident and data-driven; Emphasized technology moat (sensorless) and regulatory tailwinds; Transparent on risks (surveyed investors); Conservative on specific forward-looking product revenue splits but aggressive on volume trends.
non-obvious takeaways: Sensorless technology eliminates physical sensors entirely (not just reduces count), solving reliability issues (water/dust ingress) in EVs and enabling ISG in wet-magneto engines where competitors fail; ISG+EFI integration creates a 'hard to argue against' economic proposition for OEMs despite potential single-source hesitation.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
